architecture.mechanism: Pooling many small units into one integrated aggregate produces greater power/capacity than any single unit can deliver alone, and smooths unit-level heterogeneity (weakest-unit limitations).
architecture.intervention: Rebuild the drill battery pack as a modular multi-bank array: several smaller cell modules wired in parallel with an active balancing controller and current-sharing bus, so heavy-load current is split across all modules instead of stressing one string; add a supercapacitor buffer at the output port to absorb transition surges at load onset.
architecture.expected_effect: Sustained heavy-load output through a full shift with markedly lower per-cell current and heat, because aggregate capacity is pooled across modules and no single cell carries the full load, slowing capacity fade.
architecture.falsification_test: Run the multi-bank pack and a baseline single-string pack of equal nominal capacity on identical heavy-load drilling duty cycles; log per-cell current, temperature, and capacity retention over a full shift and 500 cycles. Hypothesis is falsified if the multi-bank pack shows no measurable reduction in per-cell stress/temperature and no slower fade, or if balancing leaves cells outside a set tolerance (e.g., >50 mV divergence).

challenge.kill_reason: all deterministic checks passed; the adversarial gauntlet's objections are ESCALATED (uncalibrated attacker, Art. L) and ride the record for adjudication
